title: Quarterly roadmap: experiment matrix and commitment lanes for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: Define a clear, testable quarterly roadmap for Hosted API + Model Catalog that separates exploratory experiments from commitment lanes (features we will guarantee for the quarter).

Scope: This ticket captures the top-level experiment matrix (hypothesis, metric, guardrails) and maps feature commitment lanes to OKRs, required engineering work, and rollout windows. It spans Hosted API surface changes, model lineup adjustments, and console-facing telemetry/rollout controls.

Background/Problem: We need to be explicit about what we will 'try' vs what we will 'ship' this quarter to reduce cross-team context-switching and set predictable expectations for customers on model availability and SLA changes. Past quarters mixed experiments into the primary commit lane which created rollback risk and vagueness in capacity planning.

Goals: 
- Produce an experiment matrix of 9–12 experiments with owners, hypotheses, success metrics, and abort criteria.
- Define 3 commitment lanes (Core Hosting SLA improvements, Model Catalog Curation & Deprecation, Canary/rollout instrumentation) with concrete deliverables and release windows.
- Map each commitment to OKRs and visible sprint milestones for PM/ENG/DX.
- Produce a risk register and dependency map tied to ENG tickets and infra capacity.
- Build a lightweight runway cost model (tokens/second & expected infra spend delta) for committed changes.

Approach and Definitions: 
- Experiment: Time-boxed work with a single primary metric (e.g., median latency @95th percentile, embedding cost per 1M ops, hallucination regression on eval set). Each experiment must include a pre-defined abort condition and one rollback plan.
- Commitment lane: Scoped feature or operational change that the organization pledges to deliver or document fallback for during the quarter. Commitments include QA gates and canary windows with automated rollback triggers.
- Commitment windows: Fixed calendar slots where canaries are allowed to graduate. We will publish a public (internal) schedule that stakeholders can rely on.

Experiment Matrix (summary rows):
- E1: Adaptive batching policy (owner: eng-rt). Hypothesis: Dynamic batch sizing reduces cost per token by ~12% without increasing p95 latency > 10%. Metric: cost/token delta; p95 latency. Abort: sustained p95 > baseline + 10% for > 1 hour.
- E2: KV cache sharding heuristic (owner: infra). Hypothesis: shard-aware cache reduces cold-start tokens by 20%. Metric: cold-start token count. Abort: >5% error increase in small-model requests.
- E3: Catalog auto-prioritization for canary models (owner: PM). Hypothesis: automated candidate selection increases positive canary pass rate by surfacing healthier variants. Metric: canary pass/fail ratio.
- E4: Quantization profile A/B on dedicated pool (owner: applied-ml). Metric: latency and output-similarity score.
- (See Confluence doc for full matrix and detailed success criteria: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/PM-142208+Experiment+Matrix)

Commitment Lanes (high level):
- Lane A — Hosted API Reliability Sprint: p95 latency SLO improvements, runtime kernel tweaks, 2 rollout windows (2026-03-25, 2026-04-08). Deliverables: runtime-1.21 canary, tracing hook instrumentation, SLO dashboard.
- Lane B — Model Catalog Health & Curation: deprecate 3 low-usage variants, publish replacement mappings, model-version pinning UI in console. Deliverables: deprecation campaign, migration guide, console flag.
- Lane C — Canary & Rollout Controls: structured canary scheduler, automated fallback to compatible variant, per-route cost cap. Deliverables: canary controller v1, per-route budget UI, playbook.

Acceptance Criteria: 
- Each commitment lane has an owner, prioritized engineering tickets, and an explicit canary schedule.
- Experiment entries have defined metric dashboards populated and at least one baseline measurement.
- Runway model updated with cost delta and capacity plan and validated by infra.

Risks and Mitigations: 
- Risk: Model deprecation causes customer breakage. Mitigation: opt-in beta and a 6-week migration window + compatibility mapping.
- Risk: Batching changes increase variability at p99s. Mitigation: strict abort criteria and short canary windows at low traffic.
- Risk: Infra capacity shortage during canary. Mitigation: reserved burst capacity allocation for canary windows (work with Dedicated finance).

Stakeholders/Approvals: 
- Necessary approvers: Head of Product (Carlos Mendes), Head of Engineering (Priya Shah), Applied ML lead (Jonah Lee), Security (if changes touch inference keys).

Deliverables and Timeline (quarterly cadence): 
- Week 1–2: Finalize matrix, baseline metrics captured, infra capacity sign-off.
- Week 3–6: Run 6–8 experiments in parallel (time-boxed), run lane A canary window 1.
- Week 7–10: Stakeholder review, iterate on experiments that meet success; abort or extend marginal experiments; canary window 2 for Lane A.
- Week 11–12: Finalize commitments, publish release notes for model catalog changes, schedule deprecation notifications.

Links and Artifacts: 
- Experiment templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/Experiment+Playbook
- Runway/cost model spreadsheet (View): drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/hostedapi-runway
- Example PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9812 (batching prototype)

Next steps for assignee: 
1) Schedule cross-functional kickoff (PM/ENG/DX/Applied ML/Infra) by 2026-03-05.
2) Create per-experiment ENG tickets (linked in dependencies) and assign owners.
3) Publish the internal canary calendar and collect SLA sign-offs.

Notes: This doc deliberately separates the commitment lanes (predictable work we will deliver) from experiments (what we will explore). The objective is to reduce downstream risk and make the roadmap a reliable planning artifact for GTM and enterprise customers.
